newsitem.title: FRANCE: Pasqua urges shift from French labour to sales tax.
newsitem.headline: Pasqua urges shift from French labour to sales tax.

text.p: Former Interior Minister Charles Pasqua said in an interview published on Thursday that he favoured shifting the social welfare burden from labour charges to a sales tax to boost employment in France.

Pasqua, campaigning for the centre-right RPR-UDF coalition for the May 25-June 1 parliamentary election, told the newspaper Les Echos that such a shift would draw production investment to France, while the consumer would come out roughly even.
An advance copy of the interview was sent to Reuters.
Pasqua also said the French people should be consulted once again on the Maastricht treaty for a single European currency because a newly drafted stability pact is not part of the treaty.
"From the moment that the conditions for the establishment of the euro are different from what was envisaged, I think it's normal to ask the French people what they think," he said.

Pasqua said a single currency made sense only if all 15 European Union members, including Britain and Italy took part and if a political body was established as a counterweight to the European central bank.
